tasks.short: Check both parties' tickets against the seat plan, settle the seating dispute or other concern, find a free seat, tell the box office of the move, and note the incident in the shift report.

steps.what: Usher checks the tickets of both parties against the seat plan
Usher settles seating disputes and helps solve other customer concerns
Usher finds a free seat by asking the box office by radio
Usher tells the box office which seat the patron moved to
Usher notes the incident in the paper shift report

tasks.design: The usher's handheld scans both tickets and shows from the ticketing system ({ECOMMERCE}) which seat each is for and whether one was resold or printed twice. It also shows free seats, so the usher does not radio the box office; once the usher has chosen a seat, the move is booked in the ticketing system. Incidents go in a short form on the handheld. Talking with patrons and settling the dispute stay with the usher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Tickets were read by eye and free seats found by radio with the box office.
tasks.enabler_now: Ticketing systems show seat status on handheld scanners.
tasks.still_hard: Upset patrons want a person, not a screen.
tasks.human_edge: Calming two families who both believe the seats are theirs.

reach.learn: Whether radio calls during shows fall.

evidence.claim: Convious runs one back end for web shop, gate till and kiosks with live reporting across channels.

assumptions: Boundary: from the seat complaint to the incident note; refunds are outside.
Input contract: seat status from the ticketing system; fallback is radio with the box office.
research_questions: Are disputes settled before the show starts more often?

incremental.description: Usher reports scanner faults to the box office.

approvals.approved_version: The new seat as chosen by the usher in s3.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small venue with few disputes; high: a large venue with many resold tickets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hear patrons' questions, give directions inside the venue, give information about local attractions, transport and parking, and look up times or ask colleagues.

steps.what: Patron asks for directions or local information
Usher gives directions to points in the facility
Usher provides information about local attractions, transport and parking
Usher looks up transport times or asks colleagues by radio

tasks.design: The e-ticket and a page on the venue website ({CMS}) carry a venue map, the nearest exits, toilets and bars per seat block, and departure times of the last trains and buses, with QR codes on signs pointing to the same page. Fewer patrons need to ask, and the usher reads times from the same page. Giving directions in person stays with the usher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Every question about routes and transport came to the usher.
tasks.enabler_now: E-tickets and venue pages can carry maps and live transport times.
tasks.still_hard: Many patrons ask a person rather than look at a phone.
tasks.human_edge: Walking a lost child back to their seat.

reach.task: Find the way at an event
reach.learn: Whether patrons use the venue page.

evidence.claim: E-tickets and venue web pages can carry maps and links to live public transport times.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patron's question to the answer; guiding patrons in an evacuation is outside.
Input contract: venue map kept by the venue; transport times from the public transport feed; fallback is asking the usher.
Patrons who look up the page instead of asking spend about the same time; priced as customer time.
Directions in person do not change.

incremental.description: Usher reports wrong information on the venue page.
Patrons look up maps and transport times on the venue page.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: an older audience that asks in person; high: a younger audience used to e-tickets.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take intermission orders and payment at the refreshment stand, serve drinks and snacks, fetch refreshments for the press box, count the takings, and send the takings report to the bar manager.

steps.what: Patron orders and pays at the refreshment stand
Usher operates the refreshment stand during intermission, taking orders and payment
Usher serves drinks and snacks
Usher obtains refreshments for press box patrons during performances
Usher counts the cash and checks the stand's takings sheet
Usher hands the takings sheet to the bar manager

tasks.design: Patrons can pre-order intermission drinks with their e-ticket in the venue's web shop ({ECOMMERCE}) and pick them up at a marked counter; at the stand a card-only till takes the rest, so fewer orders and no cash are handled in the rush. The till totals the takings; the usher checks them and, once checked, the report goes to the bar manager. Serving and fetching refreshments for the press box stay with the usher.
tasks.previous_blocker: All orders were taken and paid at the stand in a short intermission, and takings counted by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Venue web shops take pre-orders with the ticket; card-only tills total takings.
tasks.still_hard: Intermission rushes still pile up at the counter.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a queue friendly when the bell rings.

evidence.claim: Convious runs one back end for web shop, gate till and kiosks; the vendor says up to 65% of guests self-serve.

assumptions: Boundary: from the patron's order to takings reported; stock ordering is outside.
Input contract: menu and prices set by the bar manager; pre-orders from the web shop; fallback is cash at the stand.
Patrons who pre-order spend about the same time as ordering at the stand; priced as customer time.

incremental.description: Usher sorts out pre-orders picked up by the wrong patron.
Patrons pre-order drinks with their e-ticket.

approvals.approved_version: The takings as checked by the usher in s5.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few pre-orders and many cash payers; high: most patrons pre-order or pay by card.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check press passes against the accreditation list, compare the photo or ID with the person, permit or refuse entry, phone the press office about people not on the list, and log refusals.

steps.what: Usher verifies credentials of patrons against the printed accreditation list
Usher phones the press office about people not on the list
Usher compares the photo or ID with the person
Usher permits only authorized persons to enter the press box
Usher writes refused entries in the log

tasks.design: Press passes carry a QR code; the usher's handheld scans it against the live accreditation list ({OTHER}) and shows the name, photo and valid dates, including accreditations the press office adds during the event, so fewer calls are needed. Refusals are logged on the handheld. Comparing the photo with the person and deciding entry stay with the usher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Names were looked up on a printed list that missed late accreditations.
tasks.enabler_now: Accreditation systems issue QR passes that scan against a live list.
tasks.still_hard: A borrowed pass looks valid on the scanner.
tasks.human_edge: Refusing a well-known face politely when they are not on the list.

reach.learn: Whether late accreditations reach the door in time.

evidence.claim: Accreditation systems can issue QR passes that scan against a live list with photo.
Names and photos of accredited people are personal data under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from the press pass to the refusal log; issuing accreditations is outside.
Input contract: accreditation list kept by the press office; fallback is the printed list and phone.
Journalists show a QR pass instead of a paper one; no added effort.
research_questions: Do calls to the press office fall?

incremental.description: Usher handles passes that fail to scan.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small press box with familiar faces; high: a large event with many late accreditations.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The usher keeps settling disputes, helping patrons, serving and deciding who enters; radio calls, printed lists, cash and paper reports shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An usher with more time for patrons who need help.

job.title: Ushers, Lobby Attendants, and Ticket Takers
